Hi Kenji,  I have been following you off and on since my daughter, a transplanted MapleLeaf resident from Yonkers, NY gave me a heads up on your appearance at the Book Larder several years ago.. I missed your visit  but we are frequent visitors to Seattle from the east coast, specifically Fremont where we rent a little place so we can visit the grand kids whenever we want. We were just in Seattle and I actually forged some hook knives for use in my spoon carving projects with Tom Henscheid at the Port Townsend School of Woodworking at Fort Warden. Tom is a national treasure and a great teacher. I was a little disappointed that you didn't talk at all about the type of steel or the edge properties of theses knives. I never buy things after reading about them on social media posts since the products are usually disappointing but this might be an exception. How can I find out more about these knives?

For everyone bashing Kenji for "selling out", it's his product and he's using part of the proceeds for charity. In what way is he "selling out"? Who is he "selling out" to? Sure he wants to make some money, most of what he does isn't great income, but he's not taking on some shady sponsorship or something.
Also, to anything bitching about the price, I dare you to find something with the same quality, made in the US, with a similar or lower price tag. Sure it's more expensive than what you might normally buy, but it's also much higher quality. I was expecting way more expensive, so I'm very happy to see it's relatively affordable, even if it is a bit more of a luxury.
